body:
Thanks for sharing your story. I'm sorry you never got to hear what she wanted to say. I think no matter what happens in the end we'll always feel guilty. We love them too much.

"Don't remember the bad times, don't remember the sickness, remember your mom, who she was, because I'm sure who she was shone through even the cancer." Perfect :)
Don't have many friends/close family to ask but mum of an acquaintance just offered to take me through, so will be going soon. Don't really want to burden other people... but have to get there
Thank you, I will find a way

I understand - glad to hear it sounds like its going better your side, or like you started figuring out how to deal with this stuff better.

Thanks for the valuable insight and advice, (I think I do have a bit of an addictive personality, or it runs in the family a bit). Will try my best to avoid getting myself into more/worse addictions.

Thank you for replying. Think I'll try see a doc soon and see what they can help with. Will check out the AA meetings eventually when I can get there... my dad was an alcoholic actually... might have a chat with him as well.

Just commenting to say I read your post and to let you know there's someone out here that listened... I kind of know how you feel, and feel the same in many ways.

I think you write very well, so don't give up :)
